case.title: The clear-shifts question shows on Board and Tech View only
case.custom_preconds:
Setup (manual QA tester and Claude session)

Preconditions

  1. Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · Schedule access · about 15 minutes.
  2. Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  3. User: [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  4. Browser: desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  5. Location: one location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  6. People: two eligible technicians at this location: [Tech-A] "Esther Howard" and [Tech-B] (e.g. "Ralph Edwards"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  7. Data: customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Prompt Where" (used by this case only) with one Approved work order [WO-1] led by [Tech-A].
  8. Data: a shift for [Tech-A] on [WO-1] tomorrow 8:00–12:00 (entire work order).
  9. Note: Esther Howard is named in the expected results and stays as written; the other name and the number are examples.
case.custom_steps:
1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Prompt Where" in Search.
  3. Drag the card from [Tech-A]'s column into [Tech-B]'s column. Note whether the prompt opens, click Keep shifts.
  4. Drag the card back into [Tech-A]'s column.
  5. Use More actions > Reassign lead technician and click [Tech-B] in the list. Note the prompt, click Keep shifts.
  6. Move it back to [Tech-A] the same way.
  7. Use More actions > Unassign. Note the prompt, click Keep shifts.
  8. Drag the card from the Unassigned column back into [Tech-A]'s column.
  9. Pick Tech View and repeat steps 3 to 8 with the row (drag between groups, then the row's More actions).
  10. Open the work order page and change Lead Technician from [Tech-A] to [Tech-B] there.
  11. Pick List in the display switcher and look for any way to change the lead from a List row.
  12. Open the Schedule for tomorrow.
case.custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Steps 3, 5, 7 and 9: The prompt opens 6 times: Board View drag, Board View dialog, Board View Unassign, Tech View drag, Tech View dialog and Tech View Unassign.
  • Steps 10 and 11: Changing the lead on the work order page does not show the prompt, and the List offers no lead change at all, so no prompt appears there either (as today).
  • Step 12: Esther Howard's 8:00–12:00 shift is still on the Schedule (every choice was Keep shifts or no prompt).

What you should see today (build v26.40.8-7a95011, 10/8/2026): changing the lead (by dragging the card or with Reassign lead technician) shows no question about scheduled shifts, even when the outgoing lead has a shift booked for the entire work order. The lead changes at once with the "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") message, and the outgoing lead's shift stays on the Schedule. (1) If you see exactly that, mark the case Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results above say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD "Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options", Confluence 845185030, version 68 (19 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), S4-R31, read 19 Oct 2026. PO decision Chris Ward 6 Oct 2026; DR-33 (List gets no lead reassignment). Source-verified 19 October 2026.

Known problem (SV-11524, open; seen on staging by the designer on 19 Oct 2026): the message after a lead change reads "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") and has no Undo button. (1) If you see exactly that, mark this test Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R31: “The prompt shows on Board View and Tech View, when dragging, from the lead technician dialog and with Unassign. Changing the lead technician on the work order page or from the List does not show it, as today.”

Not yet checked against a build in this wording.

changes.label: Preconditions
changes.old_value:
1. Sign in to the Work Orders build under test as a user whose role has Work Orders view and Work Orders create and edit. To check: Settings > Roles & Permissions > open the role > Work Orders (an Owner or Admin role has both).
  2. Use a desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  3. In the top bar, pick the location you will test in (e.g. "Heavy Duty") and stay in it for the whole case.
  4. At least 2 technicians are eligible at this location (e.g. "Esther Howard", "Ralph Edwards"). A staff member is eligible when Clockable is on, the staff record is Active, the role is neither Office nor Time Clock User, and they are enrolled at this location. To add one:
    • Settings > Staff > add a staff member, enter a first and last name (e.g. "Ralph Edwards") and an email.
    • Pick a role that is not Office or Time Clock User (e.g. "Technician"), turn Clockable on, keep the record Active, enrol the staff member at this location, then Save.
  5. Create a customer used only by this case so a search shows only its work orders: Customers > New Customer, name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co"), add an asset with a unit number and year/make/model (e.g. unit "TRK-118", "2022 Freightliner M2"), then Save.
  6. Create the work order: Work Orders > New Work Order > pick the case customer (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") and its asset > create it, and write down its number (e.g. "S1-702").
    • On the work order page set Lead Technician to "Esther Howard".
    • On the Lines tab click New Line, enter a name (e.g. "Brake inspection") and labor hours (e.g. 2.0), and save the line.
    • Click the line's Approve (check) button so the work order status reads Approved.
  7. On the Schedule, give "Esther Howard" a shift on the work order tomorrow 8:00–12:00: Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto Esther Howard's row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · Schedule access · about 15 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.

  • Two eligible technicians at this location: [Tech-A] "Esther Howard" and [Tech-B] (e.g. "Ralph Edwards"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Prompt Where" (used by this case only) with one Approved work order [WO-1] led by [Tech-A].
  • A shift for [Tech-A] on [WO-1] tomorrow 8:00–12:00 (entire work order).
  • Esther Howard is named in the expected results and stays as written; the other name and the number are examples.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] = "Esther Howard" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it), [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Prompt Where" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Prompt Where": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-702): Lead Technician = [Tech-A].
  6. On the Schedule, give [Tech-A] a shift on the work order tomorrow 8:00–12:00: Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto [Tech-A]'s row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.
  7. Check the setup worked: on the Schedule for tomorrow, [Tech-A]'s row has the 8:00–12:00 shift on [WO-1], and [WO-1] shows Lead Technician [Tech-A]. If not, fix it before starting.

1. Open Work Orders, click the All tab and pick Board View in the display switcher (right side of the toolbar; tooltip "Board View").
  2. Type the case customer's name (e.g. "ZZ Board Test Co") in Search.
  3. Drag the card from Esther Howard's column into Ralph Edwards' column. Note whether the prompt opens, click Keep shifts.
  4. Drag the card back into Esther Howard's column.
  5. Use More actions > Reassign lead technician to pick Ralph Edwards and confirm. Note the prompt, click Keep shifts.
  6. Move it back to Esther Howard the same way.
  7. Pick Tech View and repeat steps 3 to 6 with the row (drag between groups, then the row's More actions).
  8. Open the work order page and change Lead Technician from Esther Howard to Ralph Edwards there.
  9. Pick List in the display switcher and look for any way to change the lead from a List row.
  10. Open the Schedule for tomorrow.

changes.label: Preconditions
changes.old_value:
Preconditions

  • Needs: 1 user · 1 browser · Schedule access · about 15 minutes.
  • Build: the Work Orders QA build (sv10043, v26.40.8-7a95011).
  • [User-A] = you: an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch the Admin quick-login user, shown as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit.
  • Desktop browser window at least 1024 px wide. Narrower windows show only the List, without the display switcher.
  • One location for the whole case, shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); everything below is created in this location.
  • Two eligible technicians at this location: [Tech-A] "Esther Howard" and [Tech-B] (e.g. "Ralph Edwards"). A person only counts as a technician here when the staff member is active (not deactivated), Time Clock is on, the Role is neither Office User nor Time Clock User, and this location is picked in their Location field.
  • Customer "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Prompt Where" (used by this case only) with one Approved work order [WO-1] led by [Tech-A].
  • A shift for [Tech-A] on [WO-1] tomorrow 8:00–12:00 (entire work order).
  • Esther Howard is named in the expected results and stays as written; the other name and the number are examples.

Setup

  1. Sign in as an Owner/Admin user (on a QA branch: the Admin quick-login button on the sign-in page; you appear as "Admin ShopView"). The Admin role holds Work orders > View and Work orders > Create & Edit (to check: your initials at the top right > Settings > Roles & Permissions > Admin > Work orders).
  2. Use one location for the whole case: it is shown in the top bar next to the bell (e.g. "Staging Heavy Duty - 9919"); to change it click your initials at the top right > Change Location.
  3. Settings (your initials at the top right > Settings) > Staff: reuse a technician only after checking it is active, has Time Clock on, a Role other than Office User or Time Clock User and this location in Location; otherwise add one: New Staff Member > First Name and Last Name, an Email, Role "Technician", at least one Department (required), Location = this location, Time Clock on > Save & Close. Record them as [Tech-A] = "Esther Howard" (use exactly this name: the expected results name it), [Tech-B] (e.g. Ralph Edwards).
  4. Create the customer used only by this case: top menu Customers > New Customer > Name "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Prompt Where" > Save. On the customer page click the Contacts tab > New Contact > First Name and Last Name > Save (a new asset needs a contact). Then click the Assets tab > New Asset > pick the Contact, then Year, Make, Model and Unit (e.g. 2022, Freightliner, M2, unit "TRK-118") > Save. Make is required; Unit can be left empty.
  5. Create these work orders for "ZZAUTOTEST F1 Prompt Where": Work Orders > Create Work Order > in the New Work Order window pick the Customer and its Asset > Save. The new work order opens with the New Line form (otherwise click New Line on the Lines tab): in "What Are You Doing?" pick a ready-made line (e.g. "Replace - Brake pot"; typed free text finds no results), turn on Line Approved so the work order status reads Approved, and click Save & Close. Write down the number the build gives the work order (on a QA branch they look like "S10043-17581"). Then pick the lead in the Lead Technician dropdown on the work order page; it saves at once. (While a work order is an Estimate its Lead technician is read-only on the work order page; give an Estimate its lead from Board View instead: the card's More actions (…) > Reassign lead technician > pick the technician > Reassign.) Leave Lead Technician empty on the ones that should sit in Unassigned.
    • [WO-1] (e.g. S1-702): Lead Technician = [Tech-A].
  6. On the Schedule, give [Tech-A] a shift on the work order tomorrow 8:00–12:00: Schedule > go to that day > drag the work order from the work order list onto [Tech-A]'s row at the start time > in the picker choose Entire work order > set the end time > save.
  7. Check the setup worked: on the Schedule for tomorrow, [Tech-A]'s row has the 8:00–12:00 shift on [WO-1], and [WO-1] shows Lead Technician [Tech-A]. If not, fix it before starting.

changes.label: Expected Result
changes.old_value:
Expected results

  • The prompt opens 4 times: Board View drag, Board View dialog, Tech View drag and Tech View dialog.
  • Changing the lead on the work order page does not show the prompt, and the List offers no lead change at all, so no prompt appears there either (as today).
  • Esther Howard's 8:00–12:00 shift is still on the Schedule (every choice was Keep shifts or no prompt).

What you should see today (build v26.40.8-7a95011, 10/8/2026): changing the lead (by dragging the card or with Reassign lead technician) shows no question about scheduled shifts, even when the outgoing lead has a shift booked for the entire work order. The lead changes at once with the "Lead technician updated" (or "Lead technician removed") message, and the outgoing lead's shift stays on the Schedule. (1) If you see exactly that, mark the case Failed and raise nothing new. (2) If it fails in a different way, that is a new problem: report it. (3) If it behaves as the expected results above say, the change has shipped: mark it Passed and tell the QA lead.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043; story SV-10047 (Story 4, Reassign or unassign the lead technician); PRD Confluence 845185030, edited 7 Oct 2026 (status line "PRD v33"), S4-R31, read 8 Oct 2026. PO decision Chris Ward 6 Oct 2026; DR-33 (List gets no lead reassignment). Source-verified 8 October 2026.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-R31: “The prompt shows on Board View and Tech View, both when dragging and in the Reassign dialog. Changing the lead technician on the work order page or from the List does not show it, as today.”

Last checked against build v26.40.8-7a95011 on 10/8/2026.
